example.generated_text:
### S1-5 – Targets related to own-workforce impacts, risks and opportunities

Air France-KLM considers safeguarding employee health and safety a major priority and an area in which there can be no compromise. The Group’s approach is based on evaluating and analysing existing and emerging occupational risks and deploying appropriate prevention measures. Air France’s proactive Health and Safety Policy is supported by a consolidated Health and Safety Manual, relevant key performance indicators and an Integrated Management System connecting workplace health and safety with other risk-management and continuous-improvement processes.

Occupational-accident reduction objectives are incorporated into management arrangements. Through target-based contracts, Executive Vice-Presidents formalise commitments to reducing occupational accidents by means of prevention plans. These commitments reflect the specific circumstances of the activities concerned while remaining consistent with the Company’s principal objectives. More broadly, annual target-based contracts are signed between the relevant Executive Vice-President or Vice-President and the CEO, monitored twice annually, and used to establish collective and individual targets. Progress is reported to Management Committees, reviewed through regular strategic updates by the Air France Executive Committee and considered through a dedicated Health and Safety Management Review.

The indicators used to monitor workforce impacts include absenteeism due to illness and workplace accidents, the frequency rate of workplace accidents with lost time, accident severity, training hours per employee, employees with disabilities, gender representation and signed collective agreements. Social reporting covers Air France in France, HOP!, KLM in the Netherlands and KLM Catering Services. Differences between French and Dutch definitions of work-related accidents may affect comparability and are considered when interpreting results.

For 2019, five employee fatalities were reported under both the combined indicator for work-related injuries and work-related ill health and the indicator for work-related injuries. Five fatalities were also reported for non-employees under the combined injury and ill-health indicator. This compares with zero fatalities reported in 2018 for employees and non-employees under the combined indicator, and zero employee fatalities from work-related injuries. The available information does not provide a disaggregation that would permit the combined 2019 employee and non-employee figures to be added without possible double counting.

Air France’s Diversity Charter provides a formal commitment to better reflect the diversity of the French population within its workforce and to combat all forms of discrimination. However, no quantified, time-bound diversity target, baseline or target year was reported for 2019. Similarly, although accident-reduction commitments form part of management contracts, no consolidated Group-level numerical health and safety target or defined 2019 target threshold was disclosed. Accordingly, performance is monitored through management reviews and workforce indicators, but progress against a quantified S1-5 target cannot be stated for the reporting year.

Environmental indicators for air operations: CO2 emissions per passenger and per km, Total fuel consumption and CO2 emissions, Emissions of NOX and SO2 low altitude, Global noise energy indicator. (2) Environment: Air France in France and KLM Schiphol for ground operations; Air France, HOP!, KLM and KLC for air operations. Social: Air France in France, HOP!, KLM in the Netherlands and KLM Catering Services. (3) Collective labor agreements signed in 2018, Results in terms of skills development, Results from the Employee Promotor Score related to employees engagement, Measures to reduce the Group’s impact on climate change, Measures to reduce noise impact, Anti- corruption mechanisms, Results in improving accessibility for people with disabilities, Data protection and cybersecurity mechanisms.

Annual target- based contracts are signed between the division’s Executive Vice- President or Vice- President and the CEO. Their monitoring takes place twice a year. These targets are also used for the setting of collective and individual targets. The Corporate Safety Committee within the KLM Board of Directors meets every quarter to analyze the Safety indicators for KLM. The results of an in- ﬂight observation campaign, the LOSA (Line Operations Safety Audit), a practice already used by other airlines in the United States, Asia and Australia, were published at the end of 2017 and are the subject of an action plan which forms an integral part of the ongoing process to improve ﬂight safety.

Monitoring the health of employees and advising them on the existing and emerging vocational risks 4.1.3 Health and safety in the workplace Safeguarding employee health and safety in the workplace is a major priority for Air France - KLM and an area in which there can be no compromise. Evaluating and analyzing the risks then deploying the appropriate prevention measures enables the “ Trust Together ” project to be accompanied by pro-active measures in this area.

Air France is a signatory of the Diversity Charter which constitutes the formal expression of the Company’s commitment to better reﬂecting, amongst its employees, the diversity of the French population and combating all forms of discrimination. As in previous years, in 2016 the KLM Works Council was again consulted on a range of health and safety-related issues: the air quality in outstations, the in-house emergency response organization (BHV), TCP limits and diesel emissions. Furthermore, the Works Council approved a series of overall guidelines governing the reimbursement of health care costs by KLM.

Promoted by a pro- active Health and Safety Policy, supported by a consolidated Health and Safety Manual and accompanied by the relevant key performance indicators, the steering of the safety- ﬁrst approach takes the form of progress reports to the Management Committees, regular strategic updates reviewed by the Air France Executive Committee and a special Health and Safety Management Review. During the signature of target- based contracts, the Executive Vice- Presidents in each of the entities formalize their commitment to reducing occupational accidents through their prevention plans. The undertakings reﬂect both the speciﬁcities of the ﬁelds covered and consistency with the Company’s major objectives.

More generally, Air France has developed and is pursuing the deployment of an Integrated Management System (IMS), enabling synergies between all the progress- oriented and risk management approaches: thus Flight Safety, Health and Safety in the Workplace, Customer Service Quality, Operational Performance, Environment and Sustainable Development, Food Safety and Security.
